headline: Reaction-network models guide tuning of CRISPRa, riboswitch, and cell-free expression
label: Model Guided Biological Circuit Design
summary: Mechanistic and Bayesian design frameworks now address resource competition and expression context in engineered genetic parts.
synthesis: The common thread is quantitative, model-driven design of engineered gene expression systems, where predictive models replace trial-and-error tuning. A mass-action chemical reaction network for PURE cell-free transcription and translation is generalized to arbitrary proteins and validated against MGapt. A reaction-network model of CRISPR-mediated gene activation shows that gRNAs compete for dCas9 and activator, breaking the modularity assumed in multi-gRNA designs and providing a basis for tuning. For riboswitches, a deep batch Bayesian optimization framework with an ensemble neural network surrogate iteratively designs a yeast hybrid riboswitch emulating NAND logic. The new element is the explicit coupling of mechanistic kinetic modeling with learned surrogates and sequential experimental design, rather than representation learning alone.
